Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU - follow-up and next tests

Thanks again for taking time today  good call. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call highlights:
- ACME target: ~50 concurrent generation streams for inference-heavy product, p50 latency goal <200ms for mid-length prompts, spiky traffic during product launches.
- Key concerns: capacity guarantees for high concurrency, predictable unit costs, data residency (US-east), and procurement timeline for reserved capacity.
- Current eval: youre running tests against a hyperscaler endpoint (CloudCorp) and want apples-to-apples comparison with a reserved/dedicated offering.

Redwood quick summary (differences vs hyperscalers):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool, non-preemptible allocation, predictable throughput and latency (configurable SLAs).
- Hyperscalers: flexible scaling and broader cloud services, but risk of noisy neighbors, preemption on lower tiers, and less optimized model runtime for inference economics.
- Practical impact: Dedicated reduces tail latency variance and makes unit cost per token more predictable at scale; hyperscalers may be cheaper at very low utilization but can become unpredictable during peaks.

Proposed POC & tests (what we recommend next):
1) 2-week POC on Redwood Dedicated (reserved 4x A100-equiv GPUs) with traffic replay of your production traces to measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, and token-unit cost.
2) Run the same replay against your hyperscaler setup (you already have baseline) and share traces + config (batch sizes, sequence lengths).
3) We'll run an A/B test: identical model binary, same batching settings we both agree on, and produce a simple one-page comparison (latency, throughput, cost).

What we need from ACME:
- Confirmation on sample traces (anonymized) and target test windows.
- Procurement contact + preferred PO cadence so we can share a PO template and draft MSA timeline.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-overview.pdf, redwood-hyperscaler-comparison.xlsx (high-level), acme-po-template.docx (template).

Next steps / ask:
- If OK, can we kick off the POC week of 2026-06-29? Proposed kickoff: Wed Jun 30 10:00 AM PT.
- Please loop in procurement (procurement@acme.ai) if we should send a PO template now.

Thanks  Ill coordinate engineering access, environment setup, and collect the tests well run.

Best,
Markus Klein

Tom  great questions. Answers below and additional details so procurement can move forward: 

1) Capacity guarantees / SLA:
- Redwood Dedicated is non-preemptible for reserved pools (we allocate the GPUs to your account). For the configuration proposed (4x A100-equivalent), we offer a 99.9% uptime SLA on the allocation and a latency SLO for the p50/p95 targets we agree to in the kickoff.
- When catastrophic hardware failures occur we provide automatic failover to warm spares and an SLA-backed incident response window.

2) Burst behavior and billing:
- Short bursts: we can provision temporary burst capacity from our shared spare pool for short spikes (subject to availability). Burst is billed at a premium per GPU-hour.
- For sustained higher peaks we recommend increasing reserved capacity (committed). We can model cost tradeoffs for a hybrid commit + burst strategy during the POC.

3) Ballpark pricing (illustrative, subject to contract):
- Reserved 4x A100-equiv (monthly commit): ~$35,000 / month (committed)  includes reserved capacity and priority scheduling.
- Pay-as-you-go Dedicated (no commit): ~$55 / GPU-hour (example).
- Hyperscaler baseline (varies by region and preemption): ~ $6090 / GPU-hour for on-demand; preemptible options can be lower but come with preemption risk and often require autoscaling engineering.

4) Data residency & compliance:
- You can pin the Dedicated cluster to us-east. Audit logs, access logs, and model inference logs can be retained per a mutually agreed retention schedule. We support KMS integrations for customer-managed keys.

Attachments: acme-po-template.docx (PO template)  Ive attached a draft showing billing cadence and an MSA checklist. Laura, Rishi: please add anything I missed on onboarding or engineering contact.

If that looks reasonable, next steps:
- Procurement: review the template and provide PO cadence and legal contacts.
